A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same grokking-ticket study by the same authors despite the changed title. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison. Internal reporting inconsistencies do not prevent matching the work.

before.justification: v1 reports original training experiments on modular addition and MNIST, including pruning, weight-norm controls, Transformer experiments, and representation analyses in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical experiments and adds arithmetic-task comparisons, mask-similarity measurements, frozen-weight edge-popup experiments, and dead-neuron controls.

M1.justification: The original train, magnitude-prune, and rewind grokking-ticket procedure remains unchanged. v2 adds a separate adaptation of the existing edge-popup algorithm to memorization checkpoints: weights remain fixed while mask scores are optimized (Section 5.3 and Appendix G). This extends the procedures investigated without replacing the original method.

E1.justification: Modular addition and MNIST remain covered; moving their comparisons into Appendix A does not remove them. v2 Appendix A.3 adds modular subtraction, multiplication, sum-of-squares prediction, and a random-label control, providing a limited expansion within the arithmetic setting.

E2.justification: The MLP comparisons retain norm-matched dense models, random pruning, SNIP, GraSP, and SynFlow. v2 adds edge-popup from random initialization and memorization checkpoints against ordinary weight training. It omits the weight-decayed ticket comparator from the critical-pruning comparison and removes v1's Transformer pruning-at-initialization comparison.

E3.justification: v2 introduces substantial new evaluation designs: edge-popup with width multipliers 1, 4, 8, and 16, frozen checkpoints selected at 400 epochs, and pruning rate 0.6; layerwise mask similarity against the final ticket; and dead-neuron mask interventions. Appendix H newly specifies a 90% generalization threshold for Table 1. The main modular-addition modulus and 40%/60% split remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds structural-similarity analysis, frozen-weight recovery experiments, and controls testing whether removing dead neurons explains acceleration. Conversely, v1's Transformer checkpoint, pruning-rate, and no-weight-decay analyses are omitted, along with output-weight periodicity, Fourier, and entropy analyses. The retained input-weight representation analysis is largely relocated rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: v1 Section 4.1 explicitly reports three seeds, means, and standard deviations, with uncertainty bands in multiple main-text and appendix plots. v2 removes this reporting statement and presents corresponding curves without those bands. This substantially reduces uncertainty reporting; it does not establish that fewer runs were performed.

E6.justification: v2 adds results for arithmetic tasks, mask similarity, frozen-weight generalization, and dead-neuron controls. Its new 90%-threshold Table 1 reports generalization times of 566 for grokking tickets, 21497 for the base model, and 6611 for edge-popup from memorization. Some reporting also becomes inconsistent: Appendix C changes the stated fastest pruning rate from 0.7 to 0.5, while Figure 12 still shows its minimum near 0.7.

T1.justification: v2 adds a formal definition of the edge-popup score-update rule in Definition G.1. The existing lottery-ticket statement and network equations are retained in substance. No new theorem or proof is supplied; the main text's reference to 'Theorem G.1' points to an algorithm definition.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes accelerating grokking and the insufficiency of weight norms alone. v2 strengthens the central claim to eliminating delayed generalization with suitable subnetworks and adds a prominent contribution that memorization solutions can generalize through structure optimization without weight updates. These changes extend the substantive contribution beyond reframing the title.

C2.justification: v2 interprets mask similarity and frozen-weight recovery as evidence for structural discovery during grokking, and the dead-neuron controls as evidence for task-relevant structure beyond neuron removal. It also omits v1 Appendix C.4's explicit failure to find a Transformer pruning rate permitting full generalization without weight decay, removing an important qualification of the broader explanation.

D1.justification: v2 adds edge-popup implementation information but removes v1's code-access link and detailed MNIST settings, including split sizes, layer widths, initialization scale 8, and weight-decay strength 9. Appendix A.1 retains only the broad MLP/MSE description. These are material documentation losses, without establishing that the underlying MNIST settings or actual code availability changed.

R1.justification: v2 substantially revises research positioning, including an explicit first-connection claim for lottery tickets and grokking in Section 6.4. It adds literature on representation learning, mask similarity, and pruning-only approximation, including Gromov, Paganini and Forde, Malach, and Pensia. The earlier double-descent/emergent-ability and dropout discussions are removed.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, experimental narrative, and discussion are extensively rewritten around weight norms and structural discovery. Benchmark material moves into appendices, representation analysis moves into the main text, and the standalone conclusion is replaced by discussion summaries. This is substantial narrative reorganization beyond added experiments.

P2.justification: Figures are extensively redrawn and reorganized: the opening schematic disappears, the six-panel benchmark figure becomes three appendix accuracy panels, and loss and output-weight panels are removed. New structural-analysis plots and Table 1 are added. v2 also introduces mismatched captions: Figure 12 describes checkpoint/Jaccard comparisons despite showing pruning rates, and Figure 13 describes datasets despite showing dead-neuron controls.

improvement.justification: The frozen-weight intervention and dead-neuron controls strengthen testing of the subnetwork explanation beyond v1's evidence. However, v2 loses uncertainty reporting, reproducibility details, and the Transformer no-weight-decay failure while strengthening its claims. Contradictory pruning-rate reporting and mismatched captions further weaken traceability. These substantial gains and losses leave the net effect on overall quality unclear.
